steps.label: What Is a Logical Left Shift?
steps.content:
What Is a Logical Left Shift?

Think → Pair → ShareWhere does the bit in the 128 column go when every bit moves 1 place left?Show the worked answer

There is no column to its left. It is pushed out of the register and lost.

  • A logical left shift moves every bit left by the number of places.
  • Bits pushed out on the left are lost.
  • 0s come in on the right.
  • The leftmost bit (128) is the most significant bit. The rightmost bit (1) is the least significant bit.

After000101100

  • 1 place: x 2. 2 places: x 4. 3 places: x 8.

steps.content:
What Is a Logical Right Shift?

Think → Pair → ShareA left shift multiplies by 2 for each place. What would you expect a right shift to do, and why?Show the worked answer

Divide by 2 for each place: every bit moves to a column worth half as much.

  • A logical right shift moves every bit right by the number of places.
  • Bits pushed out on the right are lost.
  • 0s come in on the left.
  • Each place right divides by 2: 1 place ÷ 2, 2 places ÷ 4, 3 places ÷ 8.

Two places: 0001 0110 = 88 ÷ 4 = 22

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "the number gets smaller" not enough for a right shift of three places?Show the worked answer

It does not say by how much. The mark scheme wants the operation and the number: divided by 8.

  • Left shift of n places: multiplied by 2 for each place (2, 4, 8, 16).
  • Right shift of n places: divided by 2 for each place (2, 4, 8, 16).
  • If a 1 is shifted out, the bits are lost and the value becomes incorrect.

items.prompt: State the mathematical effect of a right shift of four places on a positive binary integer.
items.guidance: One mark each. The second mark follows on from the first: "by 16" or "by 2 to the power 4" only earns it with divide. Do not accept divided by 4.

Exam Question: Describe a Left Shift (3 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy are "describe the process" and "state the effect" different questions?Show the answer

The process is what the bits do. The effect is what happens to the value.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 3(d). A binary integer that is stored in a register in the computer has a logical left shift performed on it.

items.prompt: (i) Describe the process of the logical left shift that is performed on the binary integer.
scheme: Each / all / every value / digit / bit in the binary number is shifted / moved to the left
The left most / most significant bit is lost
A 0 is added as the right most / least significant bit
items.guidance: Any two from the list, one mark each. The answer describes what happens to the bits, not the effect on the value.
items.modelAnswer: Every bit moves left. The leftmost bit is lost.

items.prompt: (ii) State what effect this will have on the binary integer.
scheme: The binary integer is multiplied by 2
items.guidance: 1 mark for multiplied by 2 (doubled). "It gets bigger" alone earns no mark.
